articles.title: Fatih Birol: The Energy World Will Never Be the Same As Before the Iran War
articles.summary: For more than a decade, Fatih Birol has been one of the world’s most influential voices in energy markets. As the head of the International Energy Agency (IEA), he advises presidents and energy ministers; CEOs follow his view of the market with careful attention. When we caught up at the United Nations climate change conference, known as COP31 , currently underway in Antalya, Turkey, he offered a blunt analysis: the war in Iran has unleashed a structural shift. articles.title: Breaking Down the Ending of Jessica Chastain's Nashville Thriller Heartland
articles.summary: Netflix's Heartland follows Misty Jones ( Jessica Chastain ), a former country music star living in self-imposed exile who returns to Nashville after her niece, an up-and-coming singer named Charlie Heart (Carter Faith), goes missing. As she investigates the disappearance, Misty uncovers a series of suspicious connections involving Charlie's manager, Roy Combs ( Garrett Hedlund ), and a local police detective. articles.title: Inside Salish and Jordan Matter’s Growing Father-Daughter Empire
articles.summary: It’s already 10:27 p.m. on a Saturday night in October when Salish Matter asks gently, “Are we going to start filming soon?” The 16-year-old stands in the aisle of her local Target in Manhattan Beach, Calif., beside her father Jordan Matter. They are dressed almost identically, in jeans and black shirts. articles.title: How Texas’ Blue Takeover Could Soon Begin Impacting Texans’ Lives
articles.summary: Texas has long been led by Republicans, from its governor’s mansion and state legislature down to many of its locally held offices. But this year’s elections have abruptly turned the ruby-red state blue , with sweeping implications for Texas’ laws and the lives of its more than 30 million residents. articles.title: What An Early Polar Vortex Combined With El Niño Means For Winter Weather
articles.summary: A record-early breakdown of the polar vortex is expected to bring cold weather to the United States by the end of the month. The expected wobble in the polar vortex that sends Arctic temperatures south, however, could be in competition with the strong El Niño forecast for this winter —but experts say that how it will impact our weather remains to be seen.
